hook_text: It is called a cool box, but it is just as good at keeping pap hot. Here is why.
clip_script: Heat always flows from hot to cold, by touching, by moving air or by invisible waves. A cool box slows all three. Its walls are packed with foam, which is mostly tiny bubbles of trapped air, and still air barely passes heat on. The tight lid stops air sneaking in. The white plastic bounces sunlight away. But the foam does not know which way the heat is going. Put cold drinks inside and it slows heat getting in. Put hot food inside and it slows heat getting out. Same trick in your jersey, your ceiling and a bird's fluffed-up feathers. Trap the air, slow the heat.
visual_style: Whiteboard cutaway of a cool box with foam bubbles, arrows of heat trying to cross and slowing down; then the same box flipped with hot food inside and arrows pointing the other way; quick sketches of a jersey and a fluffed bird.
pacing: Surprising hook, a steady explanation, a quick-fire finish.
